items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default — effectively the only — form: The housing stock is overwhelmingly single-detached houses on rural and agricultural lots; homes are effectively all freehold farm and rural residential lots. Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 applies, including the Section 200 agricultural zones: in the Agricultural One Zone (A1) the minimum subdivision lot area is 8.0 ha and in the Agricultural Two Zone (A2) it is 16.0 ha — the lot's zone for a single parcel is shown in the City's WebMap. Zoning at that scale does not produce subdivision lots or condo buildings.
A designation is not an approval and no site is listed as inventory here.

ALR vs non-ALR split: rural Aberdeen parcels are in or beside the Agricultural Land Reserve. No percentage is published, so no split figure is given. Subdivision, non-farm use and added dwellings on an ALR parcel need both City zoning compliance and, where the ALR Use Regulation requires it, Agricultural Land Commission approval.

Added dwellings on farm lots (the Aberdeen substitute for "more units"): the City-hosted A1 zone section permits one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit per lot in accordance with the ALR Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. These are farm dwellings, not strata lots, and cannot be sold separately.

Servicing: rural residential lots outside the urban boundary may use wells and onsite sewage rather than community water and sewer — per-parcel servicing is confirmed from the parcel's well record (provincial GWELLS) and its onsite-sewage filing, not assumed from the address.
Floodplain: Zoning Bylaw Schedule E sets floodplain boundaries.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: "Aberdeen" is both the board sub-area name in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report and an official City name — profile area 6 in the City's 2020 Demographic Profiles, separate from Bradner – Mt. Lehman (area 1) and West Abbotsford (area 7).

Nearby areas: Bradner and Mt. Lehman to the west and northwest, Abbotsford West / Clearbrook to the east, Poplar to the northeast, and Aldergrove (Township of Langley) further west along Fraser Highway.

Main roads and commute: Bradner Road (north–south through the area), Fraser Highway (north edge), Mt. Lehman Road to the west, and Huntingdon Road and King Road to the south toward YXX and the Huntingdon / Sumas border crossing; Highway 1 is reached via the Mt. Lehman Road and Clearbrook Road interchanges to the north — the route west toward Langley, Surrey and Vancouver and east toward Chilliwack.

Schools: Aberdeen Elementary, 2975 Bradner Road, is the public elementary school physically inside the sub-area (Ministry-listed name/address). Catchment, single-address only: the recorded SD34 locator run for 2975 Bradner Road (the school's own address) returns Aberdeen Elementary → Eugene Reimer Middle → Rick Hansen Secondary; Eugene Reimer Middle's family-of-schools page lists Aberdeen Elementary among its feeder schools and names Rick Hansen Secondary (Grades 9–12) as that family's secondary school. Ministry-listed addresses for the chain: Eugene Reimer Middle School, 3433 Firhill Dr (in Abbotsford West, recorded only as the middle school's address, not as an Aberdeen sample). Catchment areas are set under SD34 Policy 18.

Libraries: Mt. Lehman Library, 5875 Mt. Lehman Road (northwest), and Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way (east), both Fraser Valley Regional Library. Nearest hospital: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Road; nearest urgent and primary care centre: 100-2692 Clearbrook Road.
OCP: Abbotsforward 2050, the CURRENT Official Community Plan, governs; there is no Aberdeen neighbourhood plan

Abbotsford has a Supreme Court registry. Court-ordered sales and foreclosure matters for Aberdeen land can run through the Supreme Court registry in Abbotsford itself — relevant context for any court-sale acreage purchase.

The airport's height rules are drawn on a City map, not in the listing. The AZR area is shown on City drawing M-500; a tall shop or barn planned without checking that drawing can fail at the permit stage, after NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals are already owed.

The second Abbotsford tax penalty lands September 16, not early September. Taxes due July 2, 2026; 5% on July 3, 2026 and a further 5% on September 16, 2026 — a farm closing straddling those dates carries any unpaid penalty in the adjustments.

blocks.text: What buyers paid in Aberdeen, November 2025 to October 2026 (Paragon closed sales)
The middle half of the 29 houses that closed in Aberdeen sold between $1.26M and $1.48M. Typically they had 5 bedrooms, a build year around 2010 and a lot of about 6,487 square feet.
For houses in Aberdeen that meant a median 26 days on the market, 97.5% of the asking price, 0% going over asking and about $388 a square foot of living space.

Quarter by quarter, the typical house in Aberdeen went for $1.38M in February to April, $1.34M in May to July and $1.27M in August to October. February to April was the firmest stretch and August to October the softest.
The middle half of the 14 townhomes that closed in Aberdeen sold between $668,750 and $723,250. The typical one had 3 bedrooms, a build year around 2019 and a strata fee near $291 a month.
For townhomes in Aberdeen that meant a median 25 days on the market, 97.9% of the asking price, 0% going over asking and about $457 a square foot of living space.

Aberdeen: streets and boundaries

items.t: Aberdeen is a rural community in the City of Abbotsford around Bradner Road, south of Fraser Highway and west of Clearbrook, north of the Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) lands.
Bradner and Mt. Lehman lie west and northwest, Abbotsford West and Clearbrook east, Poplar northeast, and Aldergrove (Township of Langley) further west along Fraser Highway.
No exact boundary roads for the Aberdeen sub-area are published in text form on a City source; the Bradner Road / Fraser Highway framing is the sourced orientation.

blocks.text: Aberdeen: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is single-detached houses on rural and agricultural lots; the area is rural in character with working farm parcels, under Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014.

Homes are effectively all freehold farm and rural residential lots; the only strata housing confirmed inside the wider board sub-area is the Lantern Park townhome complex at 27640 Lantern Avenue, at the western edge by the Aldergrove border.

blocks.text: Aberdeen: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Reg. 30/2019, or as approved by the Agricultural Land Commission, on a lot of at least 0.4 hectares, to a maximum floor area of 90 square metres on lots of 40 hectares or less and 186 square metres on lots over 40 hectares, plus one secondary suite per lot to a maximum of 100 square metres.
Zoning Bylaw Schedule E sets floodplain boundaries; whether a single Aberdeen lot is in the floodplain is a lot-by-lot check in the City's WebMap.

blocks.text: Aberdeen: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Aberdeen Elementary, 2975 Bradner Road, is the only school confirmed physically inside the area; there is no middle or secondary school inside Aberdeen.
The nearest libraries are Fraser Valley Regional Library branches outside the area: Mt. Lehman Library, 5875 Mt. Lehman Road, and Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way.

Rural lots outside the urban boundary may be on wells and onsite sewage rather than community water and sewer; the City does not charge water or sewer utility fees to properties not connected to City infrastructure.
Huntingdon Road and King Road run south from the area toward Abbotsford International Airport and the Huntingdon / Sumas border crossing corridor.

blocks.text: Aberdeen: getting around

items.t: Route 21 Fraser Hwy is the area's bus service, on Fraser Highway at the north edge, between Aldergrove and Bourquin Exchange via Highstreet Exchange.
Highway 1 is reached northbound via the Mt. Lehman Road and Clearbrook Road interchanges.

blocks.text: Aberdeen: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the lot's zone and floodplain designation in the City's WebMap before offering: Zoning Bylaw Schedule E floodplain boundaries are lot-specific and do not follow from the street address alone.

For a well, look up the well record in the Province's GWELLS registry; for septic, Fraser Health states an onsite sewerage system must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation and be filed by an Authorized Person.

On Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) parcels, subdivision, non-farm use and added dwellings need both City zoning compliance and, where the ALR Use Regulation requires it, Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR status is parcel-specific.
Airport height surfaces are a separate check from zoning: a lot can be zoned for a tall farm building and still be capped by the Airport Zoning Regulations on City drawing M-500.

faq.a: There is no subdivision-lot product to buy — no named bare-land subdivision offering, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering exists here. What trades is fee-simple farm and rural residential parcels, at agricultural scale (A1 subdivision minimum 8.0 ha; A2, 16.0 ha).
faq.q: Can I buy a bare building lot in Aberdeen?

faq.a: Neither. It is a City of Abbotsford community and board sub-area: the rural ground around Bradner Road, south of Fraser Highway and west of Clearbrook, north of YXX — profile area 6 in the City's own demographic profiles, separate from Bradner – Mt. Lehman and West Abbotsford. Aldergrove (Langley) is further west along Fraser Highway.
faq.q: Where exactly is Aberdeen — is it part of Langley or Mission?

faq.a: Price subdivision expectations from the zone, not the frontage: A1 lots subdivide at a minimum of 8.0 ha and A2 at 16.0 ha, and on ALR land subdivision also needs Agricultural Land Commission approval. Confirm the parcel's zone in the City WebMap and its ALR status before valuing any split.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a farm parcel here?

faq.a: In the A1 zone, one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit per lot under the ALR Use Regulation (or as approved by the ALC), on a lot of at least 0.4 ha, to 90 m² on lots of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on lots over 40 ha; one secondary suite per lot (to 100 m² in the A1 section; Abbotsford's general suite cap is under 50% of the principal unit, coach/garden 15% of lot to max 100 m²). It is a farm dwelling — it cannot be stratified or sold separately.
faq.q: Can a second home be added for family or farm workers?

faq.a: Where the lot is inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area on City drawing M-500, yes: height may not exceed the approach, outer or transitional surfaces, and NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals are needed before a City building permit. Per-lot status must be checked — it does not follow from the street address alone.
